newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Toll sees tight rates near term.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Toll sees tight rates near term.

text.p: General freight carrier Toll Holdings Ltd believed the medium term outlook for general freight rates would be fairly tight due to highly competitive conditions, company secretary Bernard McInerney told Reuters.
The longer term outlook was more positive, McInerney said.

"We believe the Australian transport industry will continue to rationalise and as that rationalisation continues, which we have been a large part of in the last 12 months in particular, we believe that some sanity might come back into the market place," he said.
Australia's general freight sector is highly competitive due to the low barriers to entry into the business which sees a large number of owner-drivers operating on very thin margins.
McInerney put a rough five-year time frame on the rationalisation and said when it occurred then rates would improve in conjunction with a rise in economic activity.
Toll Holdings has been the emerging company in the general freight sector in the last year following the exit of most of Australia's major transport groups.
Earlier this year, Brambles Industries Ltd sold its four general freight businesses to Toll Holdings Ltd for A$25 million.
Last year, Mayne Nickless Ltd sold its general freight operation, Interlink, to Toll for about A$15 million.
Toll reported a net profit to A$5.4 million in the year to June 30, 1996 on sales of A$234.3 million. The company has forecast its 1996/97 revenue at A$472.6 million and net profit at A$9.6 million.
Part of Toll's strategic plan was to service the full distribution chain to its client base rather than outsourcing to third parties, McInerney said.

"We're sticking to our knitting. We are a niche operator and we're staying within that niche. A lot of transport companies within Australia outsource large segments of the distribution chain and we are certainly building on the fact that we can do it all ourselves," he said.
The freight that Toll carries is predominantly palletised or unitised and the company operates time sensitive deliveries to adjoining states.

"We're not in the parcel market and have no immediate plans (to get into this market). But if the opportunity was there to once again to service our clients for their total needs, then we would give that some consideration," McInerney said.
Toll's shares were up three cents at A$2.40 around 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), just below their year-high of A$2.48 and well above their year low of A$1.16.
